newsitem.title: UK: BT mum on FT report, says MCI review ongoing.
newsitem.headline: BT mum on FT report, says MCI review ongoing.

text.p: British Telecommunications plc on Tuesday declined comment on a report that there will be no major changes in the terms of its $28.7 billion merger with MCI Communications of the United States.
A BT spokesman would only say that BT's review was continuing into the merger, which was thrown into doubt in July after MCI warned of $800 million losses this year because of tough domestic markets.
"As usual we will not comment on (the merger) but only to say that the review is ongoing," a BT spokesman said.

The Financial Times reported on Tuesday that the terms of the merger were not expected to be changed except for some changes in the MCI strategy aimed at appeasing BT shareholders worried about the deal.
Citing New York securities lawyers, the FT said the merger would be approved this week by the U.S. Federal Communications Commission.
But the BT spokesman said FCC approval was not expected until "sometime in the autumn".

The newspaper said the wording of a Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filing last week of MCI's regular 10-Q quarterly financial report provided evidence that "no substantive changes in the terms have been discussed".
It quoted a U.S. securities lawyer as saying that MCI would have been obligated to indicate in the report a change in the acquisition price of the BT linkup.
According to the FT, the MCI filing said the merger should be completed by the fall 1997.
